extracted.intended_audience: Investigators preparing NIH Research & Related (R&R) Senior/Key Person profiles and NIH-style biographical sketches for grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and form fields for completing the Research & Related Senior/Key Person Profile (Expanded) and the NIH-format Biographical Sketch (for PD/PI and senior/key personnel) including required attachments and section structure. Useful for assembling personnel pages for an NIH grant application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research & Related Senior/Key Person Profile (Expanded) — required fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete the Senior/Key Person Profile (Expanded) with all profile fields (e.g., Prefix; First Name*; Middle Name; Last Name*; Suffix; Position/Title*; Organization Name*; Department; Division; Street1*; Street2; City*; County; State*; Province; Country*; Zip / Postal Code*; Phone Number*; E-Mail*; Project Role*; Degree Type; Degree Year; etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach Biographical Sketch and Attach Current & Pending Support (file upload fields). Include credential/eRA Commons user name if requested. Provide accurate contact and organizational information and indicate Project Role (e.g., PD/PI, Co-Investigator, Consultant). The form shows example entries (Professor and Chief, The Regents of the Univ. of Calif., U.C. San Diego, Pediatrics, Infectious Diseases) and file-name placeholders for biosketch and current & pending support. Follow form-required fields marked with asterisk (*).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attach Biographical Sketch (required attachment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Senior/key person must have an attached biographical sketch file (Attach Biographical Sketch*: File Name:).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload the biographical sketch PDF (example file names shown such as Biosketch_Liu.pdf). The biographical sketch must follow NIH format and length constraints described in the BIOGRAPHICAL SKETCH instructions (see separate criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attach Current & Pending Support (required attachment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Senior/key person must attach a Current & Pending Support document (Attach Current & Pending Support: File Name:).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide up-to-date current and pending support documentation as a file upload. Example shows a tracking number reference for the application. This attachment documents other active or pending funding that may affect effort or overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: BIOGRAPHICAL SKETCH — overall format and length
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the following information for the Senior/key personnel and other significant contributors. Follow this format for each person. DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the NIH biographical sketch structure and keep the entire biographical sketch to 5 pages or fewer. The document should include the labeled subsections (A. Personal Statement; Publications directly relevant to this proposal; B. Positions, Scientific Appointments, and Honors; C. Contribution to Science) as exemplified in the sample biosketch content.

rubrics_metrics.name: BIOGRAPHICAL SKETCH — A. Personal Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise Personal Statement describing the major goal of the research program, the applicant's role and qualifications for the proposed project, relevant past collaborations and roles, and a brief justification of the applicant's suitability for the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State how the applicant will contribute to the project (e.g., specific expertise, leadership roles), mention relevant collaborators or transitions (e.g., replacing a prior co-PI and arrangements to ensure seamless transition), and note continuity plans (e.g., consultants remaining on project during transition). Include a short list or pointer to publications directly relevant to the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: BIOGRAPHICAL SKETCH — Publications directly relevant to this proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: A selective list of publications that are directly relevant to the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite a small number of key publications (with full citation information and PMIDs if applicable) that demonstrate relevant prior work or expertise. These citations are listed immediately after the Personal Statement in the sample.

rubrics_metrics.name: BIOGRAPHICAL SKETCH — B. Positions, Scientific Appointments, and Honors
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a chronological list of positions and scientific appointments and a list of honors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List training (residency, fellowship), academic appointments, administrative roles, and honors/awards with dates. The sample shows positions with date ranges and an enumerated honors list. Include memberships or service on study sections as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: BIOGRAPHICAL SKETCH — C. Contribution to Science
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe major contributions to science in a numbered format; for each contribution provide a narrative description and key representative citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each numbered contribution, give a concise narrative of the scientific advance or research theme, explain its significance, and list representative publications (with citations and PMIDs/PMCID where relevant). Sub-items (a., b., c., etc.) can be used to list supporting publications. Use this section to frame the applicant's track record and relevance to the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources — describe available research space, equipment, and core resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Document facilities and resources available to support the proposed research, including laboratory space (square footage), biosafety level (e.g., BSL-2), and detailed lists of major equipment and core facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide site-specific descriptions and inventories of equipment (examples given: freezers (-80, -20, 4°C), CO2 tissue culture incubators, centrifuges, thermal cyclers, real-time RT-PCR, automated growth curve systems, spectrophotometers, plate readers, liquid handling robots, microscopes, flow cytometers, cell sorters), describe specialized rooms (darkroom, walk-in cold room, autoclave/glasswash), indicate access to additional core equipment (refrigerated superspeed centrifuges, ultracentrifuges, liquid nitrogen storage), state total research space and BSL level (example: 1477 square feet, fully functioning BSL-2), and list core/flow cytometry resources (e.g., list of cytometers and their capabilities). Use specific models/names to demonstrate capability and readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources — site-specific equipment lists
rubrics_metrics.description: For each site participating in the proposal, provide detailed inventories of equipment available in relevant dedicated laboratories (e.g., microbiology lab, molecular epidemiology and serology lab, immunology lab, cell culture and sample processing lab).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize equipment lists by lab/room with bullets for each piece of equipment (examples in the text include incubators, biosafety cabinets, centrifuges, spectrophotometers, vortexers, cell separators, plate readers, qPCR instruments, Luminex instruments, sonicators, AKTA purification system, Maxwell RSC, controlled-rate freezers, cryostorage). Include cold storage specifics (-80°C, -20°C, 4°C, liquid nitrogen) and monitoring systems. Provide details on flow cytometry/ cell sorting capacity (number and models of cytometers, lasers, detection capabilities, sorting modes, plate load options).
